Source contracts: src/agent_runtime/resource_access.py

src/agent_runtime/resource_access.py

Python · Tier A

Compile source-reviewed resource identities and match task-local consent to concrete invocations. Resource descriptors retain tool/CRUD contracts, every supplied boundary dimension and canonical path scope; they describe candidates without granting access. AccessSession revalidates checkpoint-owned grants against live policy, source and identity revisions, then supplies invocation-local receipts and Files scopes. Composite operations must cover all operands and targets. Matching performs no provider operation, while filesystem preflight can prepare the existing artifact namespace; the Gateway remains responsible for physical path enforcement.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
tool_contract 35 Extract the source-owned schema, effect, execution/completion and authorization fields used in a tool-contract digest. Descriptive catalog text and caller arguments do not become authority.
PolicyBlock 55 Carry an explicit policy owner’s denial/confirmation decision and whether task resource consent can override that owner. Tuple compatibility exposes action/reason; an arbitrary adapter exception is not a PolicyBlock.
PolicyBlock.metadata 72 Return the owner, decision, eligibility and reason for diagnostic/consent consumers without granting anything.
safe_text 139 Produce a bounded, whitespace-collapsed public label through the existing safe-error projection. This does not normalize an identity used for matching.
resource_reference 148 Digest the resource contract and identity into a stable resource_ reference, excluding presentation-only label/status/platform fields. A reference names a candidate; it is not an authorization token.
bindings 180 Cache reviewed binding metadata by registry authorization revision under a process-local lock and weak registry key. Return a deep copy on both hit and rebuild so consumers cannot alter shared cached authority descriptions.
_bindings 196 Compile supported/delegated resource operations from explicitly reviewed skill families, declared selector fields, source bindings and exposed Proxmox endpoint templates. Retain fixed CRUD arguments, tool/schema digests, policy owners and identity alternatives; an unreviewed skill raises instead of receiving inferred access.
coverage 261 Combine CRUD coverage, missing tool bindings and mismatches against the reviewed binding digests. Report gaps without altering the review manifest or automatically approving a changed contract.
selector_value 302 Resolve a declared selector or build a generated endpoint path with each substituted identity URL-encoded. Missing path parameters yield None; no provider request or endpoint discovery occurs.
canonical_path 321 Normalize a concrete path using the selected Gateway’s Windows/POSIX dialect and captured working root. Reject empty/NUL, home/environment expansion and parent traversal; relative paths require an absolute base. This is lexical matching, not filesystem or symlink resolution.
boundary 343 Collect present host/account/profile/conversation boundary dimensions from execution context. Values remain exact matching inputs rather than display labels.
make_resource 352 Freeze a known, review-matching object or explicitly requested collection into detached identity, boundary and operation metadata. Fill only unambiguous source-owned discriminators, require complete identity alternatives for objects, validate bounded scalar values and canonicalize declared paths. Unknown fields or incomplete/stale contracts raise before any consent request exists.
make_skill 416 Describe one selectable skill’s tools and used dependencies with a contract digest. A skill grant intentionally covers its tool surface without capturing a host boundary; independent target, account and file checks still apply.
tools_for 440 Collect the tool IDs named directly by a resource or by its supported operation bindings. This lookup changes neither catalog activation nor permissions.
file_operands 448 Extract every supplied Files path operand, parsing unified diffs to include each actual patch target. Invalid patches raise before access is requested; no file is opened or patched here.
matches 472 Check frozen boundaries, exact CRUD discriminators and all supplied identity dimensions for one invocation. Object grants require exact paths; explicit collections permit separator-bounded descendants. Reject symlink-following and object-level recursive/parent creation, cover additional file operands, and leave cross-Gateway copy composition to AccessSession.
AccessSession 580 Borrow task-owned in-process authority from the native run owner. Live matching rechecks policy/resource revisions and exact run identity; JSON request dictionaries cannot stand in for this class. The session never stores a new grant or edits persistent policy.
AccessSession.active 597 Return resources only from grants for the current task whose policy stamp, resource references and current source/identity revisions still validate. Revalidation reads current owners; stale or changed grants are omitted.
AccessSession.matching 618 Require the same native attempt before matching live grants. Optionally restrict to file or concrete-resource grants; cross-Gateway copies must match source read and destination write in their selected target contexts. Separate file grants can jointly cover all copy/move/diff/patch operands, but cannot expand recursive or symlink scope.
AccessSession.permits 704 Report whether any live task grant covers this exact invocation; other execution-policy owners retain their own checks.
AccessSession.permits_filesystem 709 Require matching Files resource grants rather than a broad skill/tool grant for an independent filesystem restriction.
AccessSession.file_scope 715 Project matching, nonempty file identities to exact/subtree path entries for Gateway enforcement. Return None when a concrete path scope cannot be established; this does not resolve physical aliases.
AccessSession.permits_target 728 Fence an attempt to its captured base Gateways, explicitly selected user Gateways or currently valid Gateway grants. An absent target requires no Gateway expansion; a different native_run_id is always rejected.
AccessSession.receipt 748 Derive task/grant provenance and a digest of the exact tool, arguments, run, operation and boundary only after a live match. This output describes the current authorization decision and is never accepted as authority on input.
permitted 775 Use only an actual AccessSession from Controller context for invocation consent; absent or serialized lookalikes return false.
scope_permitted 782 Require a concrete resource grant for an independently restricted scope. Broad skill/tool grants cannot supply this override.
target_permitted 792 Apply the task session’s Gateway fence when a session exists. Without one, leave the normal target-policy owner in control; true here alone does not authorize a Gateway.
filesystem_permitted 799 Check exact file-resource consent through a real session, returning false for an absent or caller-serialized session.
filesystem_policy_block 811 Identify Files operands outside the configured workspace and retained temporary/artifact namespaces when the cwd guard is enabled. Artifact namespace preparation may call the existing Gateway owner; unresolved syntax/setup failures defer to that owner rather than inventing a grant. Return a typed file_scope denial only for an established out-of-scope path; physical symlink checks stay on the Gateway.
new_task_context 892 Strip borrowed invocation/task authority and restore the captured configured base context before creating a separate task or schedule. With no AccessSession return the original context unchanged; a task grant never becomes a new task’s saved policy.
execution_context 929 Copy context only for a live session and apply invocation-local capability exposure. Remove ungranted non-base tools; a proven matching grant adds only this tool and clears its local shell- executable exclusion copy. Persistent policy, credentials and independent resource/target checks remain with their owners.
